plimpton-322.modernRelevance: The Pythagorean triples on this 3,800-year-old clay tablet use the same number-theoretic relationships that underpin RSA cryptography protecting every online transaction today.

rhind-papyrus.modernRelevance: The fraction-based algorithms Ahmes recorded are direct ancestors of the fixed-point arithmetic still used in embedded processors and GPU shaders.

democritus-atoms.modernRelevance: Every scanning tunneling microscope image of individual atoms vindicates Democritus's 2,400-year-old conjecture that matter is made of indivisible particles in void.

euclid-elements.modernRelevance: The axiomatic method Euclid invented is still how every mathematics paper, formal software verification proof, and automated theorem prover is structured today.

archimedes-method.modernRelevance: Archimedes's infinitesimal slicing technique is the conceptual ancestor of every numerical integration algorithm running in engineering simulations worldwide.

archimedes-floating-bodies.modernRelevance: Archimedes' principle of buoyancy is applied every day in naval architecture, submarine ballast systems, and the hydrometer sensors that monitor battery acid density in your car.

eratosthenes-circumference.modernRelevance: Eratosthenes's shadow-angle method is the conceptual basis of satellite geodesy, and his 2% accurate result stood as the best measurement of Earth's size for over a thousand years.

aristarchus-sizes.modernRelevance: The geometric parallax technique Aristarchus pioneered is the same method the Gaia spacecraft uses today to measure distances to two billion stars in our galaxy.

hipparchus-star-catalogue.modernRelevance: Hipparchus's magnitude system for star brightness, invented 2,100 years ago, is still the basis of the apparent magnitude scale astronomers use at every observatory on Earth.

ptolemy-almagest.modernRelevance: Ptolemy's epicycle machinery was so accurate it was used to predict eclipses and planetary positions for 1,400 years, and his coordinate system is the direct ancestor of modern celestial coordinates.

al-khwarizmi-algebra.modernRelevance: The word 'algorithm' derives from al-Khwarizmi's name, and his systematic equation-solving methods are the direct ancestor of every computer program ever written.

alhazen-optics.modernRelevance: Alhazen's camera obscura principle and his insistence on experimental verification of optical theories directly prefigure every modern camera sensor and the scientific method itself.

fibonacci-liber-abaci.modernRelevance: The Hindu-Arabic numeral system Fibonacci brought to Europe is the universal notation of global commerce, and Fibonacci numbers appear in everything from phyllotaxis to financial trading algorithms.

madhava-series.modernRelevance: Madhava's infinite series for pi and trigonometric functions, discovered 250 years before Newton, are the same Taylor series expansions computed trillions of times per second in scientific software.

copernicus-revolutions.modernRelevance: The heliocentric shift Copernicus launched is so fundamental that 'Copernican revolution' is still the metaphor scientists use when an entire field's assumptions get overturned.

galileo-sidereus.modernRelevance: Galileo's discovery of Jupiter's moons using a homemade telescope directly inspired every space telescope from Hubble to JWST and proved that observation technology can rewrite cosmology overnight.

kepler-astronomia-nova.modernRelevance: Every orbit calculation at NASA and ESA, from Mars landings to James Webb's halo orbit at L2, begins with Kepler's laws of elliptical planetary motion.

descartes-geometrie.modernRelevance: The x-y coordinate plane Descartes invented is the foundation of every graph, screen pixel grid, GPS coordinate, and data visualization on the planet.

newton-principia.modernRelevance: SpaceX's Falcon 9 booster lands itself using the same F=ma and gravitational equations Newton published in 1687 -- classical mechanics still guides nearly all space missions.

huygens-traite-lumiere.modernRelevance: Huygens's wave principle is directly applied in phased-array radar, 5G beamforming antennas, and every ultrasound machine imaging a fetus in a hospital today.

leibniz-calculus-1684.modernRelevance: The dx/dy notation Leibniz introduced in 1684 is the exact notation still taught in every calculus class worldwide and used in every differential equation solver.

euler-formula.modernRelevance: Euler's identity e^(i*pi)+1=0 is not just beautiful -- the complex exponential it represents is the workhorse of signal processing in every cellphone, MRI machine, and audio codec.

lavoisier-traite.modernRelevance: Lavoisier's insistence on precise mass measurement and systematic nomenclature established the framework every pharmaceutical lab and chemical plant on Earth operates under today.

gauss-disquisitiones.modernRelevance: Gauss's modular arithmetic is the mathematical engine inside every modern encryption system, from AES to elliptic-curve cryptography protecting billions of internet connections.

faraday-experimental.modernRelevance: Faraday's discovery of electromagnetic induction is literally what generates the electricity you are using right now -- every power plant turbine on Earth exploits this effect.

maxwell-electromagnetic.modernRelevance: Maxwell's equations govern the design of every antenna, fiber-optic cable, microchip, and wireless device -- the entire $5 trillion telecommunications industry rests on four equations from 1865.

darwin-origin.modernRelevance: Evolutionary algorithms directly inspired by Darwin's natural selection are used today to optimize everything from aircraft wing shapes to neural network architectures.

riemann-geometry.modernRelevance: Every GPS satellite computes corrections for general-relativistic time dilation using Riemannian geometry -- curved spacetime math runs in your phone's location chip.

mendeleev-periodic.modernRelevance: Mendeleev's periodic table predicted elements before they were found, and today it guides the synthesis of new materials from superconductors to cancer-targeting radioisotopes.

boltzmann-statistical.modernRelevance: Boltzmann's S=k*log(W) connects microscopic randomness to macroscopic thermodynamics, and his statistical framework underpins machine learning loss functions, Monte Carlo simulations, and modern statistical physics.

cantor-set-theory.modernRelevance: Cantor's proof that infinities come in different sizes is the foundation of modern mathematical logic, and set theory remains the axiomatic bedrock on which all of mathematics is formally built.

planck-quantum.modernRelevance: The quantization of energy Planck introduced is the reason semiconductors work, making possible every transistor in the estimated 1 trillion chips manufactured annually.

einstein-special-relativity.modernRelevance: Particle accelerators at CERN and Fermilab rely on special relativity for every beam calculation, and E=mc^2 explains why the Sun shines and nuclear reactors produce energy.

einstein-general-relativity.modernRelevance: Every GPS satellite computes corrections for general-relativistic time dilation -- without Einstein's 1915 theory, your phone's location would drift by 10 km per day.

schrodinger-wave-equation.modernRelevance: The Schrodinger equation is solved billions of times daily in computational chemistry software designing new drugs, catalysts, and semiconductor materials.

heisenberg-uncertainty.modernRelevance: The uncertainty principle sets the fundamental noise floor for every quantum sensor, and it is the reason quantum key distribution (QKD) can detect eavesdroppers.

hubble-expanding-universe.modernRelevance: Hubble's discovery that the universe is expanding launched Big Bang cosmology and is the reason the James Webb Space Telescope was built to observe the most distant, most redshifted galaxies.

godel-incompleteness.modernRelevance: Godel's proof that consistent formal systems cannot prove all truths is why no software verification tool can guarantee the absence of all bugs -- computability has hard limits.

turing-computability.modernRelevance: Every computer ever built, from your laptop to cloud data centers, is a physical realization of Turing's 1936 abstract machine -- he defined what computation means before hardware existed.

watson-crick-dna.modernRelevance: The double-helix structure Watson and Crick described is now read by sequencing machines that can decode a full human genome in under 8 hours for roughly $200.

shannon-information.modernRelevance: Shannon's information theory sets the hard limits on data compression and transmission rates exploited by every streaming service, cellphone modem, and deep-space communication link.

bell-theorem.modernRelevance: Bell's theorem proved quantum entanglement is real and non-local, and it is the theoretical guarantee behind quantum key distribution networks being deployed commercially today.

hawking-radiation.modernRelevance: Hawking radiation unified quantum mechanics, general relativity, and thermodynamics for the first time, and the resulting black hole information paradox remains the central open problem driving quantum gravity research.

perlmutter-accelerating.modernRelevance: The discovery that the expansion of the universe is accelerating revealed that roughly 68% of all energy in the cosmos is dark energy -- a mystery that DESI and Euclid are actively probing right now.

ligo-gravitational-waves.modernRelevance: LIGO's detection opened gravitational-wave astronomy as an entirely new way to observe the universe, and the LISA space detector launching in the 2030s will extend it to supermassive black hole mergers.

doudna-charpentier-crispr.modernRelevance: CRISPR gene editing, based on this paper's technique, is now in FDA-approved therapies for sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia, with hundreds more clinical trials underway.

eht-m87.modernRelevance: The first image of a black hole's shadow matched general relativity's predictions to within measurement error, providing the strongest visual confirmation of Einstein's theory in extreme gravity.

vaswani-transformer.modernRelevance: The Transformer architecture introduced in this paper powers GPT, Claude, Gemini, and essentially every large language model -- it is the engine of the current AI revolution.

alphafold-protein.modernRelevance: AlphaFold has predicted the 3D structure of over 200 million proteins, accelerating drug discovery pipelines that previously took years of crystallography down to minutes of computation.
